routes.label: Check the root domain and compare coefficients

question: What is the sum of the reciprocals of the roots of the equation \[\dfrac{2003}{2004}x + 1 + \dfrac{1}{x} = 0?\]
solution:
The denominator requires \(x\ne0\). Multiplying by \(x\) gives the equivalent equation
\[
\frac{2003}{2004}x^2+x+1=0.
\]
Its discriminant is
\[
\Delta=1-4\left(\frac{2003}{2004}\right)
=-\frac{1502}{501}<0.
\]
Thus there are no real roots, so a real-roots-only interpretation gives no pair of reciprocals to add.

If the question intends to include the two nonreal roots, call them \(u\) and \(v\). We can find the requested sum without calculating either root. Dividing the quadratic by its leading coefficient and expanding its factors gives
\[
(x-u)(x-v)=x^2-(u+v)x+uv
=x^2+\frac{2004}{2003}x+\frac{2004}{2003}.
\]
Matching coefficients shows that
\[
u+v=-\frac{2004}{2003},\qquad uv=\frac{2004}{2003}.
\]
The nonzero product ensures that both reciprocals exist. Therefore
\[
\frac1u+\frac1v=\frac{u+v}{uv}=-1.
\]
Hence \(-1\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\), is the answer conditional on including nonreal roots; there is no such pair of real roots.
